source.title: An Empirical Investigation of Pre-trained Model Selection for Out-of-Distribution Generalization and Calibration
source.authors: Hiroki Naganuma; Ryuichiro Hataya; K. Yoshida; Ioannis Mitliagkas

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no relevant truncation is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-style investigation to image models fine-tuned for out-of-distribution classification, reporting downstream OOD performance against model size and pre-training dataset size. It does not measure language-model pre-training loss.
record.gate_note: The paper reports OOD accuracy/error trends with model and dataset size, which bear on V6. Its ECE findings are recorded separately as findings not covered by a claim version. It does not report held-out pre-training cross-entropy, small-run loss extrapolations, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Individual plotted model results are not all transcribed here.
record.test_reason: Measures downstream OOD accuracy/error of fine-tuned vision models against pre-trained parameter count and pre-training dataset size. This bears on V6 (downstream gains with scale) in a new setting, image classification. It reports no pre-training loss, no fitted power laws, no extrapolation and no compute allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors report 'signs of scaling laws'. Larger pre-trained vision models and datasets improve OOD generalization and calibration after fine-tuning. Generic pre-training recipes transfer better than recipes tuned for ImageNet-1k.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fine-tuned visual classification models and OOD accuracy/error rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy; compares model and pre-training dataset sizes rather than training tokens, compute, or compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that architecture affects OOD accuracy at similar parameter sizes: ViT and ConvNeXt tend to outperform conventional CNNs such as ResNet and EfficientNet. It also reports dataset-dependent effects of fine-tuning regularization and differences between training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger pre-trained vision models and datasets give lower OOD ECE after fine-tuning. Zero-shot CLIP calibration worsens with encoder size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In visual OOD fine-tuning, calibration (ECE) improves with pre-trained model and dataset size.

fits_no_version.finding: At similar parameter counts, ViT and ConvNeXt achieve higher OOD accuracy than ResNet and EfficientNet. Architecture and recipe matter for downstream accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream OOD accuracy depends substantially on architecture and pre-training recipe at fixed parameter count.

record.problems: The study concerns image classification and downstream OOD metrics rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy. The reported scaling trends are described qualitatively; many individual results appear in plots, and the text does not provide fitted exponents or a compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.rows_left_out: Individual model-by-dataset outcomes in Figs. 3, D.5–D.7, D.17 and related architecture-specific plots are not transcribed separately; the aggregate textual findings are recorded instead. The paper also reports additional training-recipe and optimizer comparisons not extracted because they do not directly test the listed versions.

untested.parts: Language-model downstream tasks; prediction of downstream performance from pre-training loss; any fitted, quantitative predictive law (trends are described qualitatively as 'signs of scaling laws').
Power-law form of loss in vision or fine-tuning: the study reports downstream error that is 'almost linear' in log-parameters, with no loss measurement or power-law fit.
Not tested: no extrapolation from small runs.
Not tested on loss; architecture effects are on OOD accuracy only.

missing.what: Per-model OOD accuracies over three seeds. PACS ResNet-50/101/152: 82.83/88.17/89.20. VLCS ResNet: 73.91/72.72/73.73 (non-monotonic). VLCS ConvNeXt small/base: 79.61/77.93.
Exceptions to the size trend: VGG and MLP-Mixer don't follow it; EfficientNets and ResNet A1–A3 fall below the trend.
ConvNeXt-xlarge worse than smaller models on OfficeHome (Product), attributed to saturation.
Best large model vs ERM ResNet-50 OOD accuracy, e.g. OfficeHome 62.7→87.4.

record.verdict_notes: The vision setting and downstream accuracy make this only a loose, qualitative test of V6. There are no power-law fits or loss measures. The dataset-size axis is narrow and confounded with fine-tuning recipe.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pre-training loss measurements or loss scaling against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No fits from small language-model runs or predictions of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation experiments or compute-optimal scaling estimates.
Architecture comparisons concern visual OOD accuracy, not held-out pre-training loss at fixed parameter count.
The study examines vision models and fine-tuning/transfer, but does not measure the same held-out cross-entropy loss scaling form in those settings.

Tests OOD image-classification accuracy/error after fine-tuning against visual model size and pre-training dataset size; does not test language-model downstream tasks or predict performance from pre-training loss.
Does not fit or compare language-model loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations, nor analyze their sensitivity to fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuned ImageNet-pretrained vision models (ResNet, RegNet, EfficientNet, ConvNeXt, ViT) on PACS, OfficeHome and DomainNet, plus Camelyon17 and TerraIncognita
relationships.reason: Larger models and larger pre-training sets give higher OOD accuracy. OOD error falls almost linearly in log-parameters (r1, r2; Sec. 5.1, Figs. 3, D.5–D.7, D.17).
relationships.display_finding: Larger models and pretraining datasets increased out-of-distribution accuracy, with error decreasing almost linearly in log parameter count.

relationships.condition: VGG and MLP-Mixer families; VLCS dataset; ImageNet-tuned pre-training recipes (EfficientNet, ResNet A1–A3); saturated test environments
relationships.reason: Fig. 1 excepts VGG and MLP-Mixer. Table C.1 shows VLCS ResNet and ConvNeXt scaling flat or reversed. A1–A3 recipes underperform originals. ConvNeXt-xlarge is worse on OfficeHome-Product. Based on the text; rows not yet recorded.
relationships.display_finding: VGG and MLP-Mixer departed from the general trend, VLCS scaling was flat or reversed for ResNet and ConvNeXt, A1–A3 recipes underperformed originals, and ConvNeXt-xlarge performed worse on OfficeHome-Product.
